data.narrative:
Hexana is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Sylvain Nizou and Paul Gauthe that has raised €25M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 peers: three public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and eight private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Fuse Energy, and Applied Atomics operating in the nuclear energy sector.

Traditional peer-median valuation is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only four same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables, falling below the minimum threshold of three datapoints needed for statistical reliability within narrow filtering criteria. Restricting analysis to seed-stage peers or similar valuation tiers yields insufficient depth. A broader all-sector median approach would introduce material distortion given nuclear energy's distinct capital intensity, regulatory environment, and technology maturity profiles relative to other frontier-tech verticals.

The analysis therefore cannot support a triangulated valuation range at this time. The sparse peer set within nuclear energy at seed stage represents the primary constraint. Forward progress on valuation would require either: (1) additional seed-stage nuclear comparables entering the dataset with disclosed valuations, (2) application of alternative methods such as DCF or cost-of-capital approaches using company-specific technical and market assumptions, or (3) reliance on transaction multiples from prior funding rounds if available. Current data limitations preclude quantitative synthesis of a defensible range.
